name: SlateDB
tagline: Embedded LSM storage engine that writes straight to object storage like S3.
description: SlateDB is an embedded, LSM-tree key-value engine written in Rust whose SSTables and write-ahead log live in object storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob, MinIO, Tigris) instead of local disk. That gives bottomless, highly durable storage and trivial replication at the cost of higher write latency, which it mitigates by batching writes and caching reads locally. It supports a single fenced writer with many readers, snapshots and optimistic transactions, with bindings for Go, Java, Node.js and Python. Still pre-1.0 (0.17 in 2026) and governed under the Commonhaus Foundation, it is a building block for stateless-compute systems rather than a database you query directly.

pricing.notes: Free; you pay your object-store provider for storage and API requests.

scale.notes: Storage is bounded only by the object store; throughput is limited by the single writer and object-store latency.

strengths: Bottomless, highly durable storage on S3-compatible object stores
No local disks to manage; compute nodes can be stateless
Single-writer fencing protocol prevents split-brain writers
Multiple readers can scale reads from the same bucket
Bindings for Go, Java, Node.js and Python
weaknesses: Write latency in tens to hundreds of milliseconds due to object-store PUTs
Pre-1.0: APIs and formats may still change
Object-store request costs need tuning (flush interval, caching)
useCases: State backends for stream processors and serverless compute
Durable logs and queues on S3
Embedding a KV engine in diskless containers
notIdealFor: Teams needing a stable 1.0 storage format today
